messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] inv_chi_square_cdf failing on windows
parts:
On Wed, Dec 26, 2012 at 11:19 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
I missed a boost::math::gamma -- just pushed a fix.

Yeah... I tried that. I wish it were that simple.

Here's the message we're getting in Windows:
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_gamma.hpp: In function 'typename stan::return_type<T_y, T_low, T_high>::type stan::prob::inv_gamma_cdf(const T_y&, const T_shape&, const T_scale&, const Policy&)':
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_gamma.hpp:261:49: error: there are no arguments to 'gamma' that depend on a template parameter, so a declaration of 'gamma' must be available [-fpermissive]
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_gamma.hpp:261:49: note: (if you use '-fpermissive', G++ will accept your code, but allowing the use of an undeclared name is deprecated)
In file included from src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous.hpp:10:0,
                 from src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate.hpp:4,
                 from src/stan/prob/distributions.hpp:4,
                 from src/stan/model/model_header.hpp:31:
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_chi_square.hpp: In function 'typename stan::return_type<T_y, T_dof>::type stan::prob::inv_chi_square_cdf(const T_y&, const T_dof&, const Policy&)':
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_chi_square.hpp:166:30: error: 'boost::math::gamma' has not been declared
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_chi_square.hpp:177:46: error: there are no arguments to 'gamma' that depend on a template parameter, so a declaration of 'gamma' must be available [-fpermissive]
In file included from src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous.hpp:11:0,
                 from src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate.hpp:4,
                 from src/stan/prob/distributions.hpp:4,
                 from src/stan/model/model_header.hpp:31:
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/scaled_inv_chi_square.hpp: In function 'typename stan::return_type<T_y, T_low, T_high>::type stan::prob::scaled_inv_chi_square_cdf(const T_y&, const T_dof&, const T_scale&, const Policy&)':
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/scaled_inv_chi_square.hpp:208:51: error: there are no arguments to 'gamma' that depend on a template parameter, so a declaration of 'gamma' must be available [-fpermissive]

I honestly don't know what that error message is about. gamma() is called without a template parameter -- it's always called with a const double.

src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_chi_square.hpp:166:30: error: 'boost::math::gamma' has not been declared
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/inv_chi_square.hpp:177:46: error: there are no arguments to 'gamma' that depend on a template parameter, so a declaration of 'gamma' must be available [-fpermissive]
In file included from src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous.hpp:11:0,
                 from src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate.hpp:4,
                 from src/stan/prob/distributions.hpp:4,
                 from src/stan/model/model_header.hpp:31:
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/scaled_inv_chi_square.hpp: In function 'typename stan::return_type<T_y, T_low, T_high>::type stan::prob::scaled_inv_chi_square_cdf(const T_y&, const T_dof&, const T_scale&, const Policy&)':
src/stan/prob/distributions/univariate/continuous/scaled_inv_chi_square.hpp:208:51: error: there are no arguments to 'gamma' that depend on a template parameter, so a declaration of 'gamma' must be available [-fpermissive]

I honestly don't know what that error message is about. gamma() is called without a template parameter -- it's always called with a const double.

I think I got it. It's tgamma(), not gamma(). http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_52_0/libs/math/doc/sf_and_dist/html/math_toolkit/special/sf_gamma/tgamma.html

I'm running the tests on the Windows box now. I'll let you know in a few minutes if that works.


Daniel

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] inv_chi_square_cdf failing on windows
parts:
By the way, I have the experience that using gamma intended to be the gamma function in math in C on Linux, on which gamma is actually log gamma and tgamma (true gamma) should be used.  But on Mac, gamma is really the gamma in math.  So I guess we should never use "gamma" literally in C/C++.

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] inv_chi_square_cdf failing on windows
parts:
n 12/27/12 12:27 AM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> By the way, I have the experience that using gamma intended to be the gamma function in math in C on Linux, on which
> gamma is actually log gamma and tgamma (true gamma) should be used.

Where are you including them from?

We're using the lgamma() and digamma() implementations from
Boost. These should work the same way on every platform.
To make sure you get those, call:

boost::math::lgamma()

and

boost::math::digamma()

> But on Mac, gamma is really the gamma in math. So
> I guess we should never use "gamma" literally in C/C++.

I'm not quite sure what you mean by "literally".

In some cases, we have things like this in a block:

template <typename T>
...
{
using boost::math::lgamma;

T x;

T y = lgamma(x);

}

What happens here is that you get the lgamma from Boost
unless T is stan::agrad::var, in which case argument-dependent
lookup gives you the lgamma function defined in stan::agrad.

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument-dependent_name_lookup

- Bob
